speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have had a tympanoplasty and are now experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. To help me understand your current condition better, can you tell me how many days or weeks it has been since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tympanic Nerve Neuroma (or Graft Erosion) secondary to prior Tympanoplasty.

The clinical picture of shooting ear pain triggered by chewing and discomfort with earrings, despite normal imaging and audiometry, is most consistent with a neuroma of the tympanic nerve or erosion of the graft. The lack of radiating pain or jaw movement triggers makes a TMJ disorder less likely.
